text:
Monica: heads-up — platform is going to add an optional routing hint header `x-rw-fallback: true|false` to signal we should immediately route to fallback variants when capacity/quotas are tight. planning to land behind a console toggle + canary.
Eli: what does "fallback" mean here? model variant fallback or route-tier fallback?
CJ: variant fallback — e.g., if gp-large is saturated, service should route to gp-medium or an opt-quantized variant. preserves latency SLOs.
Amanda: is this purely routing or also affects billing/quotas? if we route to a cheaper variant we need to ensure cost attribution is correct.
Monica: good Q — it should preserve customer token accounting. telemetry will emit a `routing.variant` tag with original requested model and served model so billing/console can attribute.
Devex-bot: FYI: SDK changes will be required to expose the header for clients that want deterministic behavior (opt-in). we'll publish migration guide.
Mike: concern: if SDKs start auto-setting `x-rw-fallback: true` by default we risk silent semantic changes for customers. some customers rely on strict model pinning today.
Sara: agree. please keep default = absent. SDKs should expose an explicit flag: e.g., Python Client(..., fallback_policy='enabled'|'disabled'|'server'), TS same.
Eli: implementation question: do we require the console toggle to be per-route? per-model? per-tenant?
Monica: plan is per-route with optional model-level overrides. console UX: toggle + rollout % so ops can canary across 10/50/100% of traffic.
Amanda: telemetry side: we need to sample p95 latency and error deltas when fallback is on vs off. also capture failure reasons when fallback triggered (quota, capacity, backpressure).
Mike: SDK authoring: Python change will be non-breaking if we add param fallback=None which keeps header absent. but TS default undefined as well. Go has stricter signatures — will add functional options to keep backwards compatibility.
Eli: any logging format agreed? we should unify snippet for observability and console ingestion.
Monica: yes — events will include `event: routing_decision`, fields: route_attempt, reason, selected_variant, original_model. We'll add an example JSON in the docs site.
Sara: rollout plan: backend 1) accept header (no-op) 2) emit telemetry 3) apply header logic for routes with toggle. SDKs should ship opt-in flags around step 3; we need a clear announcement and 30-day deprecation window if anyone complains.
Amanda: on billing: we'll surface a usage line item for served_variant. finance is ok with that but requests a migration report for last-30-days once enabled.
Mike: test matrix: 1) SDKs opt-in flag toggled on/off 2) Console per-route toggle 3) Canary 10/50/100 4) Telemetry deltas show no spike.
Monica: action items: @Mike prototype SDK flags in py/ts/go, @Sara add telemetry hooks and dashboards, @Amanda coordinate billing contract + report, @Eli and @CJ add console toggle UX + rollout widget.
Eli: I'll mock the console UX in figma and share link.
Mike: will open PRs for python+ts (non-breaking defaults) and a go opt-in option. timeline: aiming for alpha canary next week.
Monica: thanks — please post PR links here and tag #eng-oncall for the canary window. we'll keep default behavior unchanged until step 3 and clearly communicate.
CJ: noted. adding thread to release checklist and scheduling a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk folks through rollback mechanics.
Monica: :thumbsup:
